name: the-cook
description: bin/clean fixes from tasks/prd-ralph-tui-matrix.md (#53): remove only the run's own parallel worktrees, and recognise a cherry-picked or rebased delivery.

userStories.title: bin/clean removes only its own run's parallel worktrees
userStories.description: As a developer with several runs or an earlier runner's worktrees in one clone, I want `.ralph-tui/bin/clean <name>` to remove only what run `<name>` created, so other work is never lost.
acceptanceCriteria: A test in `core/src/test/groovy/thecook/RalphTuiCookTest.groovy` fails on the 4.2.0 `clean.sh`: it creates a `ralph-parallel/*` worktree outside `.worktrees/ralph/.ralph-worktrees/<name>/` with an uncommitted file, runs `bin/clean <name>`, and asserts that worktree, its file and its branch remain.

`cookbook/ralph/bin/clean.sh` removes only worktrees whose path is under `<root>/.worktrees/ralph/.ralph-worktrees/<name>/`, and their branches; it never lists or removes others, with or without `--force`.
Without `--force`, a worktree under that directory with uncommitted changes makes `clean` exit 1 before removing anything, naming the worktree and that `--force` deletes them.
With `--force`, those worktrees are removed and each removal is printed, as today.

`cleanRemovesADeliveredRunAndEveryParallelWorktree` places its `ralph-parallel/*` worktrees under `.worktrees/ralph/demo/.ralph-tui/worktrees/`, a path ralph-tui never uses (F9), and asserts `clean` removes them; it encodes the defect. It is rewritten to place them at F9's path, and the foreign case moves to the new test. Every other `RalphTuiCookTest` test passes unchanged.

userStories.title: bin/clean recognises a cherry-picked or rebased delivery
userStories.description: As a team that delivers run branches by cherry-pick or rebase, I want `bin/clean` to recognise them as delivered, so `--force` and its skipped dirty check are not the norm.
acceptanceCriteria: `clean.sh` counts `ralph/<name>` as delivered when `git cherry <upstream> ralph/<name>` lists no line starting with `+`, where `<upstream>` is `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` when it resolves and `HEAD` otherwise.
Its refusal names the commits not found upstream and says a squash merge, or a cherry-pick that resolved conflicts, still needs `--force`.

Tests: a cherry-picked branch is cleaned without `--force`; a rebased branch is cleaned; an undelivered branch is refused; with `origin/HEAD` set ahead of a lagging `HEAD`, a branch delivered upstream is cleaned.

`cleanRefusesUndeliveredOrUncommittedWorkUnlessForced` asserts the 4.2.0 refusal text ("has commits that HEAD does not", "a squash or rebase merge"); its assertions change to the new text, and it still asserts the refusal.
